spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **load balancer** distributes incoming connections or requests across a pool of backend servers while removing unhealthy instances from rotation: **L4 (Transport)**: routes on `(src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto)` using IPVS/eBPF/Maglev at >10M packets/sec.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Virtual-Node Hash Ring for Stateful Affinity & Cache Locality (N1 -> N2 -> N3 -> N4 -> N1a); Why gRPC Requires L7 or Client-Side Load Balancing (gRPC Client -> Envoy L7 Proxy -> Pod 1 (EWMA 4ms) -> Pod 2 (EWMA 22ms)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose between packet-rate scale, protocol intelligence, and zero-hop client routing. Hyperscale architectures combine an **L4 Maglev/ECMP edge** (horizontally scaling across BGP/Anycast IPs) in front of **L7 Envoy gateways** that terminate TLS, separate `/livez`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore gRPC HTTP/2 balancing, NGINX 502 buffer tuning, and consistent hashing.

learningJourney.title: What is Load Balancing (L4 vs L7 & Consistent Hashing)
learningJourney.explanation:
A **load balancer** distributes incoming connections or requests across a pool of backend servers while removing unhealthy instances from rotation:
- **L4 (Transport)**: routes on `(src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto)` using IPVS/eBPF/Maglev at >10M packets/sec.
- **L7 (Application)**: terminates TLS/HTTP to inspect paths, headers, and gRPC frames.
- **Consistent Hashing**: maps keys (`tenant_id`, `cache_key`) onto a hash ring with virtual nodes so adding/removing a backend only remaps $1/N$ keys.

sectionDiagram.title: Virtual-Node Hash Ring for Stateful Affinity & Cache Locality
sectionDiagram.summary: Virtual nodes (150–256 per physical host) prevent hot-spot skew and ensure only ~1/N keys move on scale-out.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Load Balancing (L4 vs L7 & Consistent Hashing) works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Round Robin and L4-only fail on gRPC and heterogeneous workloads
learningJourney.explanation:
Without load balancing, one overloaded instance or AZ outage takes down the service. Even with a balancer, two classic traps spike p99 latency:
- **The gRPC / HTTP/2 Trap**: HTTP/2 multiplexes thousands of RPCs over one long-lived TCP connection. An L4 balancer pins that single TCP connection to *one* backend pod forever.
- **Health-Check Herd Collapse**: if one slow node fails `/healthz` and gets ejected, its load dumps onto the remaining nodes, knocking them out in a domino cascade.

sectionDiagram.title: Why gRPC Requires L7 or Client-Side Load Balancing
sectionDiagram.summary: L7 proxies multiplex-unwrap HTTP/2 streams and use P2C+EWMA to steer RPCs away from degraded pods.

benefits: Multi-AZ distribution, zero-downtime blue/green & canary splits, automatic outlier ejection.
costs: Adds 0.2–2 ms proxy hop and TLS termination CPU.

benefits: Route writes to the single elected primary via service discovery or PgBouncer.
costs: Spraying writes across replicas breaks consistency.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Power of Two Choices (P2C) + Outlier & Slow-Start Config
learningJourney.explanation: Envoy and Linkerd use **P2C + Peak EWMA**: sample 2 random backends and pick the one with lower active requests/latency. Pair this with `max_ejection_percent: 50` (panic threshold) and `slow_start_config` so newly booted pods warm caches gradually.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Envoy Upstream Cluster: P2C + Outlier Ejection + Slow-Start
lb_policy: LEAST_REQUEST
least_request_lb_config:
  choice_count: 2
  slow_start_config:
    slow_start_window: 45s
outlier_detection:
  consecutive_5xx: 5
  interval: 10s
  base_ejection_time: 30s
  max_ejection_percent: 50  # Panic threshold prevents cascading domino ejection
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: L4 (IPVS/Maglev) vs. L7 (Envoy/ALB) vs. Client-Side
learningJourney.explanation: Choose between packet-rate scale, protocol intelligence, and zero-hop client routing.

benefits: Handles >10M PPS with near-zero CPU; Direct Server Return preserves client IP.
costs: Cannot inspect HTTP paths/headers or rebalance multiplexed HTTP/2 connections.

benefits: Path/header routing, gRPC stream balancing, retries, and circuit breaking.
costs: Higher CPU/memory per connection due to TLS termination and HTTP parsing.

benefits: Round Robin is stateless and O(1).
costs: Round Robin ignores heterogeneous request costs (5s export vs 5ms health check).

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Two-Tier Edge: L4 Anycast/Maglev -> L7 Envoy Mesh
learningJourney.explanation: Hyperscale architectures combine an **L4 Maglev/ECMP edge** (horizontally scaling across BGP/Anycast IPs) in front of **L7 Envoy gateways** that terminate TLS, separate `/livez` from `/readyz`, and apply P2C + panic-threshold routing.

ideas.title: Separate /livez from /readyz
ideas.description: Never tie `/readyz` to downstream DB checks unless you want a DB hiccup to eject all pods simultaneously.

ideas.title: Slow-Start Warmup
ideas.description: Ramp traffic weight linearly over 30–60 s so JIT compilers and L1 caches warm up before receiving full QPS.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does an L4 TCP load balancer fail to distribute gRPC traffic evenly across newly scaled backend pods?

options.text: gRPC uses UDP instead of TCP
options.feedback: gRPC runs over HTTP/2 on top of TCP.

options.text: HTTP/2 multiplexes thousands of RPCs over a single persistent TCP connection, which L4 pins to one backend pod
options.feedback: Correct: L4 balances per TCP connection, not per RPC stream; you need L7 balancing or client-side balancing.

options.text: L4 balancers cannot route TLS traffic
options.feedback: L4 balancers forward encrypted TCP packets transparently without terminating TLS.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
